account:
Today has mostly followed my appointment book: office work, a grain inspection at the mill, lunch at home, and tea with my dockside neighbour. The mill sales chest contained eighty-two hay bales, but I did not obtain a worker's condition report. The secretary has received no new correspondence and has not located the accounts ledger or established who keeps incoming council letters.

There have been vague rumours about changes to the bridge or port. I heard townsfolk mention the bakery, baker and freight, but that is not evidence of a proposal. My neighbour likewise heard market rumours and said neither the baker nor freight could confirm them. The secretary has found no firsthand proposal evidence. I do not know whether any such change is actually planned, and have asked that concrete information reach the office.

I have now arrived in the great hall for the eighteen o'clock community gathering arranged with the innkeeper and recorded in my appointments addendum. Freight escorted me from the office, and the secretary accompanied us. The innkeeper and builder are here waiting; the builder is holding a lantern, and several lanterns are placed around the hall. These preparations seem consistent with an evening gathering. I have not yet heard its particular business, and have no grounds to connect it with the bridge or port rumours.
